content:
For too long we have tolerated axiom impurity. "It's not a priority." "We have finite resources." "Nobody cares." For too long, we have stood by and let this happen. But today is the day this atrocity ends. Today I am announcing **cLEAN** (Constructive Lean), a community fork dedicated to axiom purity.

Some say that forking an entire theorem prover over String.toList is "disproportionate." I say that accepting Classical Choice in basic string operations is what's disproportionate.

Roadmap:

  1. Remove Classical Choice from String.toList — DONE ✔
  2. Remove Classical Choice from omega when unnecessary — DONE ✔
  3. Everything else — TBD
  4. Cubical types — let's not get ahead of ourselves

Contributors welcome. Constructivists preferred. Classicists tolerated.

• I think it's a strange choice to use an LLM to meme, what's the point of memeing if it's not between humans
  • AFAIK the String API is in great flux right now, are you sure there are no plans to remove choice there / did you suggest these anywhere?
  • This fork seems to have been created yesterday, how serious is this project?
  • wdyt about #general > Make mathlib less dependent on choice (I know this is mathlib and not core)

The meme itself is human generated FWIW.

It's not a serious attempt to fork lean, but it does genuinely remove Classical Choice from String.toList by modifying omega. Interesting to note that this was done purely with AI without any knowledge of Lean internals, but this is also exactly why I didn't submit it as a PR.

If others have AI slop contributions that might not be worthy of a PR to Lean, I'd encourage you to submit it as a PR to my repo, unless anyone is aware of a WikiLean* where anyone can make changes. There's a good chance that soon AI will be able to effectively triage and make use of changes that are currently not worth human review, so it would be good to pool these .

  • I know there are some efforts in the direction of a WikiLib: sloplib, VibeRegistry, but I'm not aware of anything like this for Lean itself.
